key_insight: Adaptive Algorithmic Control (A2C) reallocates finite quantum-computing resources based on a state-derived proxy for hardness, yielding better performance than hardware-only improvements.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a software-level control strategy for quantum simulations and optimization that can boost low-energy sampling without increasing circuit depth or measurement budget.
method: State-Proxy Equalization theorem guides optimal allocation of computational effort.
Infer cumulative hardness directly from the evolving quantum state instead of reconstructing the full many-body spectrum.
Adapt resource distribution during execution to match hardness rather than physical time.
evidence_signal: Across exact simulations, supercomputer runs, and IBM hardware tests on optimization problems up to 156 qubits, A2C improved low-energy sampling probabilities by 22% to over 100,000% under matched circuit depths and measurement budgets.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate state-derived hardness estimation, which may be difficult to maintain for noisy systems or when state information is limited.
paper_title: Beyond Hardware: Adaptive Algorithmic Control by State-Proxy Equalization
